title: I left the game industry 8 years ago. Now I’m building a WWII typing shooter with AI-assisted coding.
author: Bright-Management-27
selftext:
Hi everyone! I left the game industry eight years ago. This year, I started making games again as a solo developer, working after work and on weekends.

I’m building **Words at War**, a first-person typing shooter set in **Normandy, 1944**. Every correct letter fires a shot. Movement is automatic, so the player focuses on typing enemy words and deciding which threat to deal with first.

I handle the game design, level design, and playtesting myself, with AI assistance for coding. The art uses assets purchased from the Unity Asset Store.

For this project, getting a feature working is only part of the process. I still need to play the encounters repeatedly to judge enemy timing, word readability, and whether the player can understand what went wrong. Those are also the things I’d like fresh eyes on now.

**Acts 1, 2, and 3 are playable for free in a desktop browser. A keyboard is required.**

**Play here:** [https://changhyup.itch.io/words-at-war](https://changhyup.itch.io/words-at-war)

Even a short session would help—you don’t need to finish all three acts. Was there a moment when you felt confused, frustrated, or wanted to stop? When several enemies appeared, could you tell which one to shoot first?

Comments are welcome, and there’s an optional 1–2 minute survey on the game page.

For others using AI in Unity development, I’d also be interested in how you keep changes manageable as your project grows.

Thanks for taking a look!
